quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: You cannot drive if medication impairs your driving. This is:

options.text: Allowed if you don't feel drowsy.
Allowed if a doctor prescribed it.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance. This includes alcohol, prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: This sign means the road ahead:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road will curve to the right first, then to the left.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic light or sign, you should:

options.text: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors for nearby traffic before stopping. Be aware of other drivers. Release the accelerator and move your foot to the brake. Press smoothly for a gentle stop.

questions.question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the street instead of at a crosswalk, you:

options.text: Do not have to stop for them.

questions.explanation: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally.

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection:

options.text: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
Oncoming traffic and pedestrians must yield to you.
You never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
questions.explanation: When turning left, yield to traffic going straight. Always yield to pedestrians.

questions.question: Safe driving on interstate highways requires:

options.text: The ability to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.explanation: Interstate driving requires you to stay alert and be able to drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: You must remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Only the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must see clearly through all windows before driving. Clear snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors.

questions.question: When a traffic signal is not working, you should:

options.text: Come to a full stop and yield before entering.
Go through if it looks clear.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and yield before entering.
questions.explanation: Treat a broken traffic signal as an all-way stop. Stop completely, look, and yield the right-of-way before entering.

questions.question: If you see an animal on the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down and stop if safe. Swerving can cause you to lose control and crash.

questions.question: A construction site flagger signals you. You should obey:

options.text: Only if you see orange cones.
Unless they conflict with signs or laws.

questions.explanation: Always obey flaggers at construction sites. They help keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the road means:
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. When both yellow lines are solid, no one can pass from either direction.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure all passengers buckle their belts.

questions.explanation: Buckle your belt and make sure all passengers buckle theirs before starting the engine.

questions.question: When driving in fog, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off the weather and make it harder to see.

questions.question: You have a green light and pedestrians are in the intersection. You:
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, even with a green light. Always yield to pedestrians when turning.

questions.question: This bicyclist is signaling:
questions.explanation: Bicyclists use hand signals instead of turn signals. A straight left arm means they are turning left.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:
questions.explanation: Obey flaggers at construction sites. They keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Anything that requires quick action while driving.
Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
Anything that makes you focus more on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving means anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving. It is the main cause of crashes. Distractions cause you to miss important signals and cues that help prevent crashes.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle:

options.text: When a police officer orders you to stop.

questions.explanation: Stop at a red traffic light. Always obey police officers directing traffic, even if signs or signals say otherwise.

questions.question: You must obey school crossing guards:

options.text: Unless you do not see any children.

questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. They help keep children safe.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you:
questions.explanation: Keep the same speed when being passed. Do not speed up. Let the other vehicle safely move back into your lane.

questions.question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
questions.explanation: Drowsiness harms your judgment just like alcohol and drugs. It slows your reactions, lowers your awareness, and makes driving unsafe.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop (like school buses and hazmat trucks).
Watch for trains from both directions.

questions.explanation: Be very careful at railroad crossings. Watch for vehicles that must stop there, like school buses and hazmat trucks. Make sure no trains are coming from either direction before you cross.

questions.question: Night driving is harder because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Night driving is difficult because you can only see as far as your headlights go. It is hard to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are going.

questions.question: This sign warns you of:
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. It is posted a few hundred feet before the tracks. Slow down, look, listen, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers to be alert. A side road will join the road ahead.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, you should:

options.text: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop to rest or let someone else drive.
questions.explanation: Tiredness slows your thinking and reactions. Stopping to rest or changing drivers is the safest choice.

questions.question: Which of these dangerous driving practices is also illegal?
questions.explanation: It is illegal to wear headphones in both ears while driving. You need to hear traffic sounds and emergency vehicles.

questions.question: On a wet or icy road, you should:
questions.explanation: On wet or icy roads, your tires do not grip as well. Reduce your speed to stay safe.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep downgrade ahead. Check your brakes before going down the hill.

questions.question: Smoking in a vehicle with someone under 18 is:

options.text: Legal if it is your child.

questions.explanation: It is illegal to smoke in a vehicle when anyone under 18 is present.

questions.question: You must report a traffic accident in California when:

options.text: Your vehicle fails a smog test.
Someone is injured in the collision.

questions.correctAnswerText: Someone is injured in the collision.
questions.explanation: Report any collision to the DMV within 10 days if anyone was injured or killed. This is required even if you did not cause the crash or if it happened on private property.

questions.question: Alcohol and drugs affect which driving skills?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs slow your nervous system. They reduce your alertness, increase reaction time, and harm your coordination.

questions.question: Which statement about blind spots is true?

options.text: One mirror eliminates all blind spots.
Large trucks have bigger blind spots than cars.
The rearview mirror shows all blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Large trucks have bigger blind spots than cars.
questions.explanation: Even with all mirrors, blind spots exist. Large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:
questions.explanation: When turning left, let oncoming traffic go first. Turn only when it is safe and you will not block oncoming vehicles.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
Always brake suddenly to stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Apply brakes gently with steady pressure to stop smoothly.

questions.question: Using a cell phone while driving is distracting because:

options.text: You worry about the call cost.
It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off the road.
Other drivers notice you using it.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your hands, eyes, and mind off the road.
questions.explanation: Cell phone use is dangerous because it occupies your hands, eyes, and mind. Even skilled drivers increase their crash risk when using a phone.
